routes.title: Our Story – Slopes to Hope
routes.bodyText: Skip to content Slopes to Hope Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope Menu CloseHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATE Our Story At a Glance: Founded: April 3, 2025- 17,803 lbs Recovered & Redistributed in Year 1- 23 Hotel & Ski Resort Partners- 28 Nonprofit & Community Recipients- Serving Colorado CommunitiesSlopes to Hope was founded by Drew Roberts after working in Summit County's hospitality industry and seeing firsthand how much usable winter clothing was being left behind each ski season. How it started While working at the Grand Lodge on Peak 7, I saw firsthand how much winter clothing guests left behind each ski season. For years, these items were donated to the local FIRC thrift stores until those stores closed. When I heard about this at our Rotary Club meeting, I started thinking about all the clothing that would no longer have a place to go.One question kept coming to mind:"What are we going to do with all these clothes?"I reached out to local nonprofits, but none could use that volume of clothing. Through Rotary, I was connected with Christ's Body Ministries in Denver, a homeless shelter that could put the clothing to use helping people in need. I then approached several hotels and resorts in Summit County with a simple proposal:"Instead of throwing these items away, let me pick them up and deliver them to this shelter in Denver that can get them directly to people in need."Six hotels agreed. During the 2023–2024 ski season, we recovered and distributed 3,052 pounds of winter clothing to Christ's Body Ministries. Seeing the impact of those donations showed there was an opportunity to expand the program.It also raised another question: "What if more hotels participated?"Slopes to Hope was created to answer that question and officially became a Colorado nonprofit on April 3, 2025. Where We Are Today As of September 2026, 23 hotels and ski resorts throughout Summit County have partnered with Slopes to Hope. During our first full year as a nonprofit, we recovered and redistributed 17,803 pounds of clothing, blankets, linens, and other useful items.Those donations have been distributed to 28 nonprofit and community organizations serving Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs.What started with one question has become a growing network of hotel partners, volunteers, donors, and nonprofit organizations working together to reduce waste and help people across Colorado.This is what Slopes to Hope is about:Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope. "I believe there is a strong will among the people of this world to help those in need. And if they are given the opportunity and resources, I believe they will." - Drew Roberts, Founder Copyright © 2026 Slopes to Hope

routes.bodyText: Skip to content Slopes to Hope Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope Menu CloseHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATE Recovering More Than Clothing — Restoring HopeSlopes to Hope is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Breckenridge, Colorado. We partner with local hotels and ski resorts to recover clothing items lost or left behind by guests and visitors, diverting thousands of pounds of waste from Colorado landfills. These high-quality clothing items are then distributed to homeless shelters, churches, schools, and nonprofits across Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs—getting essential gear into the hands of Coloradans facing economic and housing hardships. DONATE! Newsletter Signup Since December 2023… 25,599 pounds - Collected and RedistributedWinter coats, gloves, boots, snow pants, hats, blankets, bed pillows, dishes, books... 23 - Resort and Hotel Collection PartnersSummit County lodging establishements, public donation drop-off locations, thrift stores with surplus donations... 28 - nonprofit and community partnersHomeless shelters, nonprofits, churches, and schools throughout Colorado communities.Media9NEWS Follow-up – story by Matt Renoux9NEWS – story by Matt RenouxSummit Daily – article by Kit GearyBreckenridge Magazine – article by Lisa BlakeUnofficial Networks – article by Francis XavierKeystone Resort – video by Jake Marquardt View Reel on InstagramBy @keystone_resort Make a tangible and measurable impact!Make a measurableand tangible impact! We are raising $25,000 during our second year to help us reach our goal of collecting and distributing 20,000 pounds of winter clothing.Help us divert thousands of pounds of usable clothing from landfills and provide winter clothing to Coloradans experiencing homelessness and hardship! $8,068.03 0% GIVE NOW! Pledge-per-Pound Volunteer Partner Fundraising Goal (2027) – $25,000 $8,068.03 0%ImpactGoals & HistoryCurrent GoalCollect and distribute 20,000 pounds during the 2026-2027 ski season!Goal:4,743/20,000 0%Pounds collected and distributed during the 2025-2026 ski season.Goal:17,803/10,000 0%Clothing Donation Drop-off Locations U.S. Bank – Breckenridge (map)Inside the main door of the building to the left – before entering the U.S. Bank suite Lincoln West Mall – Breckenridge (map)Main floor against the column near Main St. entrance Connect Breck Building – Breckenridge (map)Inside south entrance door Main Library – Frisco (map)Across from main desk North Branch Library – Silverthorne (map)Inside main entrance to the left of the doors South Branch Library – Breckenridge (map)Right of the stairs by the main desk MissionOur mission is to reduce environmental waste and support Coloradans experiencing homelessness and hardship by collecting and repurposing clothing items lost or left behind at hotels and ski resorts. We distribute these clothes to our nonprofit partners, homeless shelters, schools, and community organizations in Summit County, the Denver Metro Area, and Colorado Springs—diverting thousands of pounds of clothing from Colorado landfills and fostering a more sustainable and compassionate Colorado community. Why? Tens of thousands of pounds of winter clothes are left behind or lost by guests at Colorado ski resorts and hotels every year. Most of these clothes end up in our landfills. There are also tens of thousands of people in Colorado who are experiencing homelessness, or cannot afford proper winter clothing. We address these two problems with one solution. How? We go to the hotels and resorts in Summit County and collect these winter clothes, and then distribute them to homeless shelters, churches, and community organizations. This keeps thousands of pounds of clothes out of the landfill and gets them to the people who need them the most. How is it funded? We are seeking funding from grants, sponsorships, and individual donors. We are also exploring different fundraising events, such as an auction for new ski equipment and apparel, or nights at participating resorts. Individuals and businesses may also pledge a penny per pound of clothing we collect and distribute. How can you help? Beyond donations, we seek help with community outreach and connecting with hotel and resort managers!We are also seeking volunteers to help us collect clothes from hotels and resorts and deliver them to shelters and nonprofit organizations throughout Colorado. Contact us! Copyright © 2026 Slopes to Hope

routes.bodyText: Skip to content Slopes to Hope Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope Menu CloseHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEF.A.Q.What does Community Across America do?Community Across America provides information and resources related to communities across America, such as local events, businesses, organizations, schools, government services, and community news. It serves as a hub for finding relevant information about communities in the United States.Focuses include:Connecting individuals, local and national nonprofits, and businesses and institutions to their communityNational focus covering communities across AmericaMultifaceted approach to community building, encompassing networking, resource sharing, engagement, and promotionEmphasis on community-driven content, potentially relying on user-generated content and engagementWhat makes Community Across America unique?While this organization focuses on many things that are already initiatives of many communities, the inclusion of a community currency will be key to increase and reward community engagement. This innovative point system can be tailored to any community across the country, rewarding individuals for their involvement with nonprofit organizations, volunteering for community events, and participation in local initiatives. With these points being redeemable at local and national businesses and institutions, it will be the driving force to increase community participation beyond the traditional practices. How will individuals in the community benefit?Networking and Connection: Community Across America will provide individuals with a platform to connect and network with other community members who share similar interests, hobbies, or goals. This can help individuals expand their social circles and build relationships with people who they may not have met otherwise.Resource Sharing: The website can serve as a hub for sharing resources and information relevant to the community. Individuals can access valuable information about local events, resources, businesses, and services, which can help them make informed decisions and better navigate their community.Community Engagement: This organization will provide individuals with opportunities to engage with their community and contribute to its growth and development. This may include participating in discussions, sharing ideas, volunteering for events or causes, or supporting local businesses.Empowerment: Community Across America will empower individuals to take an active role in shaping their community and making a positive impact. By providing tools and resources for community organizing and activism, individuals can work together to address local issues and create positive change.How will local and national organizations benefit?Increased Visibility: Community Across America will provide local and national organizations with increased visibility and exposure to community members who may not be aware of their services or activities. By listing their organization and events on the website, they can reach a wider audience and potentially attract new members or supporters.Community Engagement: The website can provide local and national organizations with opportunities to engage with community members and receive feedback on their programs and services. This can help them better understand the needs of the community and tailor their services to better serve them.Collaboration and Partnership: The organization will provide a platform for local and national organizations to collaborate and partner on initiatives that benefit the community. This can include joint events, programs, or advocacy efforts that align with their shared goals and values.Resource Sharing: Community Across America will serve as a hub for sharing resources and information relevant to local and national organizations. This can include best practices, funding opportunities, or relevant research, which can help them improve their programs and services.How will businesses, institutions, communities, and governments (sponsors) benefit?Brand Awareness: Businesses can benefit from increased brand awareness and exposure to a wider audience through their sponsorship of this program. This can help build brand recognition and loyalty among the community.Community Engagement: Institutions can benefit from increased community engagement and interaction through their involvement with the website. By sponsoring local events, contributing resources, or participating in community initiatives, sponsors can build positive relationships with community members and improve their image within the community.Targeted Marketing: Sponsors can benefit from targeted marketing opportunities through the website. By sponsoring specific events or initiatives that align with their target market or customer base, they can reach their desired audience more effectively.Networking Opportunities: Communities can benefit from networking opportunities with other sponsors, community leaders, and influencers through their involvement with the website. This can help them build relationships with other organizations and individuals who share their goals and values.Positive Community Impact: Governments can benefit from making a positive impact on the community through their involvement with the website. By contributing resources and support to local initiatives and causes, they can improve the well-being of the community and build a positive reputation among community members.Misc.Will I receive newsletters and promotional emails?No. You have complete control over all notifications and emails. We will never sell your information or add you to a mailing list. How much are Community Points worth? What can I do with them?During this pilot program, we are still exploring a value for these points. However, once instituted, points will be retroactively assigned a value and you will be able to use them in various ways. This may include discounts on groceries, concert tickets, dinner or drinks at a local bar or restaurant, ski passes, rounds of golf, discounts on gas, or coupons at local and national retailers. How do I receive credit for volunteering at an event?Those events that allow tracking of participation will have an option to register on the event page. You will be sent an email with a PDF ticket and QR code that the organizer will be able to scan at the event, confirming your attendance. Your account will be credited accordingly.Can anyone post an event to the calendar?No. If you wish to be able to post your events to the calendar, you must contact us to be verified as an organizer. This allows us to control the legitimacy of posts and the safety of participants. Is there a limit to how many events organizers can post?During our pilot program, organizers are free to post as many events as they wish.How can You help?DevelopmentCommunity Across America requires assistance with planning to create a roadmap for achieving its short and long-term goals. This includes developing strategic plans, project plans, and annual operating plans. The organization needs expertise in strategic planning, program development, budgeting, and project management. The goal is to ensure that the organization’s resources are effectively and efficiently utilized in achieving its mission of making a positive impact in communities across America. You may find more information and apply here.OperationsCommunity Across America requires assistance with developing its operations to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in fulfilling its mission of making a positive impact in communities across America. This includes evaluating and analyzing current operational processes, identifying areas for improvement, and implementing new policies and procedures. The organization needs expertise in operations management, strategic planning, budgeting, data analysis, project management, and quality assurance. The goal is to optimize operations and streamline processes to ensure smooth functioning and successful achievement of organizational objectives.You may find more information and apply here.Technology and Web Design This organization values ongoing technical development to improve its user experience, functionality, and security. This includes developing new features and integrations, improving the website’s scalability and reliability, and enhancing its data analytics capabilities.You may find more information and apply here.Community OutreachWe will need to establish partnerships with local organizations such as schools, non-profits, and businesses to help spread awareness about the website and its mission. These partnerships can help to reach a wider audience and create meaningful relationships with members of the community. This may involve creating and executing marketing campaigns, developing social media strategies, or conducting user research to better understand the needs of the community. You may find more information and apply here.FundraisingCommunity Across America will require assistance with fundraising and revenue generation efforts to support its ongoing development and operations. This involves developing grant proposals, creating fundraising campaigns, and exploring new revenue streams such as sponsorships or advertising. You may find more information and apply here.Watch Our Short VideoLearn more about our pilot program and vision! Copyright © 2026 Slopes to Hope

routes.bodyText: Skip to content Slopes to Hope Reducing Waste and Fostering Hope Menu CloseHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEHomeGalleryTeamOur StoryPartnersContactDONATEBoard of Directors Drew Roberts Founder & Executive Director | Board PresidentRestaurateur | Rotarian | Community Leader Drew RobertsFounder & Executive Director | Board President Drew Roberts is the Founder and Executive Director of Slopes to Hope. He established the organization after recognizing an opportunity to help people experiencing homelessness and hardship by recovering winter clothing left behind at Colorado hotels and ski resorts and redistributing it to people who need it most.Originally from Wisconsin, where he owned and operated restaurants, Drew brought a strong background in business operations, organization, coordination, and team leadership when he relocated to Colorado in 2022—experience that has proven valuable in building and growing Slopes to Hope.Since moving to Breckenridge, he has become deeply involved in community service and leadership, taking on a variety of roles including President of the Breckenridge Mountain Rotary Club, founder of the Tenmile Toastmasters Club in Frisco, and leadership positions within Toastmasters District 26.Today, Drew dedicates his time and energy to leading and growing Slopes to Hope, building partnerships and expanding its impact across Colorado.Email:drew@slopestohope.com Tammy KrieseTreasurerBranch Manager, U.S. Bank Breckenridge Erica Endorf SecretaryRegional Director of Operations, Sage Hospitality Group Erica EndorfSecretary Erica Endorf serves on the Board of Directors of Slopes to Hope, bringing more than two decades of hospitality experience and a genuine commitment to serving people, strengthening communities, and reducing waste.As Regional Director of Operations for Sage Hospitality Group, Erica works closely with hotel leaders to strengthen performance, develop talent, and create memorable guest experiences. Her knowledge of hotel operations offers a natural connection to Slopes to Hope’s mission of partnering with hotels and resorts to give unclaimed items a new purpose.Erica began her hospitality career as a reservationist at a beachfront hotel in South Florida and has since held progressive leadership roles with Sage Hospitality Group. Throughout her career, she has been known for her collaborative approach, optimistic outlook, and belief that the best results come from people working together around a shared purpose.Erica is proud to support Slopes to Hope’s practical and compassionate work on behalf of Colorado communities and the environment. Outside of work, Erica treasures time with her husband and twin daughters and enjoys being outdoors whenever she can. Kirk Barrell Board MemberEnergy Executive & Geologist | Founder, Barrell Energy | NuQuest2 | Amelia Resources Kirk BarrellBoard Member With an extensive forty-year tenure in the energy sector, Kirk A. Barrell stands as a seasoned industry veteran and geologist. Over the past thirty-one years, he has been a driving force behind the establishment of multiple enterprises, including Barrell Energy, Barrell Lithium, and Amelia Resources, where he serves as President. In 2021, he co-founded NuQuest Energy to focus on renewable energy project development across the Gulf Coast.For the past 19 years, Kirk has served as President of Emmaus House Inc., a Harlem-based non-profit that has supported the community for six decades.Kirk’s background in energy, renewable solutions, and sustainable development aligns with Slopes to Hope’s commitment to reducing waste and advancing a more circular approach to resource use. Drawing on decades of experience building organizations and leading nonprofit initiatives, he is passionate about supporting solutions that create lasting positive impacts for communities and the environment. Helena Robinowitz Board MemberSustainability Specialist, Arapahoe Basin Ski Area Helena RobinowitzBoard Member Helena Robinowitz is a board member of Slopes to Hope. Since moving to Dillon in 2023, she has worked as the Sustainability Specialist at Arapahoe Basin Ski Area. Through her waste diversion work in the ski industry, she has become passionate in cultivating creative ways to reduce waste and perpetuate circular economic principles in the outdoor recreation industry.She also runs the Arapahoe Basin Belonging and Wellness committees.Outside of work, she is also a board member of Eagle Summit Wilderness Alliance, as she is passionate about protecting wilderness areas, and loves to trail run, snowboard, bike, and go to shows at the Dillon Amp.Advisory Board Marty FerrisAdvisorFinance Director (Retired), Summit County Government Dave MillerAdvisorFormer Executive Director, Mountain Top Explorium | Education Foundation of the Summit Board Member Christy TurnerAdvisorUniversal Recycling Program Manager, City and County of Denver | Former Community Programs Manager, High Country Conservation Center Vicki BrentinAdvisorService Resource Chair, Rotary International District 5450 Angie LaytonAdvisorPresident, Boulder Flatirons Rotary Club Copyright © 2026 Slopes to Hope
